item.title: 15 Years Ago, Zelda Told its Most Memorable Story with its Worst Gameplay
item.description: Hold the controller over your head. The Master Sword glows. Point it at the screen, hit Y to recenter, and swing. On the screen, Link swings… kind of the right way. Then, your chatty companion, Fi, chimes in with a very long and earnest explanation of something you figured out several minutes ago. Rinse and repeat for about 40 hours, and that’s Skyward Sword , one of the most cinematic, heartrending, memorable stories Zelda has ever told — and the one saddled with the most finicky gameplay.

item.title: 'WTC win was no fluke': Temba Bavuma slams 'critics' after statement win over Australia
item.description: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma believes his team have answered questions about their World Test Championship (WTC) triumph after completing a 2-1 series win over Australia. The Proteas came back from a defeat in the opening Test to win the next two matches, including the series decider by 176 runs at Newlands on Saturday. South Africa's recent run includes qualifying for the 2025 WTC final even after forfeiting a series in New Zealand, beating defending champions Australia in the final at Lord's, drawing a series in Pakistan and winning a Test series in India for the first time in 25 years. They have now added a home series victory over Australia to that record. The win in Cape Town also took South Africa to the top of the ICC Test rankings. Simon Harmer played a key role in the victory, taking 6/16 in the second innings and finishing with match figures of 10/120. Kagiso Rabada claimed three early wickets as Australia were bowled out for 111 while chasing 288. South Africa's series win came after they lost the opening Test in Durban by 214 runs. They responded with an innings-and-31-run victory in Gqeberha before sealing the series in Cape Town. Speaking after the win, Bavuma reflected on the demands of the series and the effort required from his players to maintain their performance. "It's tough, to be honest," he said. "You wake up every day asking yourself to be at your best. Physically, there's times where you feel like you can't go at 100%, but you need to dig deep, and if the opportunity's there, make sure you're in the best mental space to make the play for the team. Even if things don't go well for you with the ball or the bat, you still need to be looking at ways as to how you can contribute within the team." — cricinfo (@cricinfo) Bavuma described the series as "15 days of just pressure". It came after South Africa had gone almost a year without playing a Test and 21 months without playing one at home. He said the opening defeat in Durban had been a "rude awakening". "There were two quality sides who came up against each other, and really forced each other to play their best cricket," Bavuma said. "It will be important for us to acknowledge what we've achieved, celebrate whatever milestones, take whatever learnings that come with it, and really bask in what we've achieved. In the two-and-a-half years, if you look at the team, we've been able to squeeze out every inch of every individual." Bavuma also hopes the team's performances will change how they are viewed by critics, who have questioned whether their WTC title was a one-off achievement. "I do hope with the way that we've performed, not the result, but the way that we've performed, it's given that belief. And I guess in a cheeky way, answer to certain critics saying that what we did at the WTC was a fluke. The sky's the limit for the team."

item.title: Enugu APC urges residents to verify political claims
item.description: By Dennis Agbo The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Enugu State has urged residents to exercise caution when receiving and sharing political information ahead of the 2027 general elections. The APC Campaign Council’s Spokesperson and Director of Public Communications, Steve Oruruo, made the appeal in a statement titled, “Unmasking the Alarmism of NDC: A Clarion Call for Enugu’s Extra Vigilance.” Oruruo referred to public discussions surrounding the management of Amadeo Event Centre and a proposed town hall meeting involving the New Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi. He said the disagreement over the use of the facility was a matter involving the parties to a private agreement and urged political stakeholders to avoid drawing conclusions about the involvement of the state government without verified information. The APC spokesperson also called on residents to verify reports, particularly those circulating on social media, before accepting or sharing them. He said political discussions ahead of the 2027 elections should focus on candidates’ ideas, policies and capacity to deliver good governance. Oruruo further highlighted the development programmes of Governor Peter Mbah’s administration, expressing confidence that the government’s record would feature prominently in the electoral contest. He urged Ndi Enugu to remain vigilant, promote issue-based political engagement and assess the proposals and records of political parties as the state approaches the 2027 general elections. The post Enugu APC urges residents to verify political claims appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘I searched and found’ – Pastor Jimmy Odukoya confirms marriage to Pastor Mo Jasmine
item.description: Former Nollywood actor turned cleric, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has confirmed his marriage to his fiancée, Pastor Mo Jasmine. Odukoya made the announcement during a church service, where he invited his new wife onto the altar and introduced her to the congregation. The confirmation comes a day after the cleric hinted that he had found love again, sharing a photograph of his and his fiancée’s hands, both wearing rings. Sharing their love story with the congregation, Odukoya said he had been searching for a suitable partner before finding his wife. “You know, the Bible said it is not good, it said I will find someone suitable. When Adam saw, he said this is the flesh of my flesh, bone of my bone, I was looking and searching, and I found. Some of you saw the post, some people said is it artwork, no it’s my wife; allow me to introduce to you for the first time, Pastor Mrs. Odukoya, a new first lady, my wife. Pastor Mo Odukoya,” he said. The marriage marks a new chapter in Odukoya’s personal life following the end of his previous marriage to Oluwakemi Sade Banjoko. The former couple got married in London in March 2013 and had two children together before their separation. Vanguard News The post ‘I searched and found’ – Pastor Jimmy Odukoya confirms marriage to Pastor Mo Jasmine appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Data Is King. Does Duke Have Alexander the Great?
item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 20: Sebastian Wilkins #5 of the Duke Blue Devils reacts following a basket during the first half of the game against the Tennessee Volunteers at Cameron Indoor Stadium on October 20, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images A s most sentient fans know, data and analytics have transformed sports. You can focus in on seemingly minute things. For instance, it might turn out that if, say, a Virginia starter tends to hit 65 percent of his shots when he goes right, but only 35 percent when he goes left, and if you can force him left X percent more than your odds of winning go up by Y percent. We do think that some coaches are overly reliant on analytics, but it’s an unavoidable revolution, because knowledge is power. Analytics can give you incredible insights into your opponent. One other hypothetical: your opponent’s big man becomes 40 percent less effective if he draws two fouls in the first 10 minutes. Basically, data and analytics can be a cheat sheet, not least of all for your own team. And as we’ve also seen, Duke coach Jon Scheyer really has his finger on the pulse of the game, and has adapted Duke’s approach. He was the first coach to hire a GM, and Rachel Baker has had a huge impact on the game. He cut a deal with Amazon Prime to broadcast three games there this season. And he hired rising star Alexander Powell. Powell, who played D-III ball, is the subject of this article from the Duke Chronicle. He’s a huge asset to Duke Basketball, and yet another savvy hire by Scheyer. Go to the DBR Boards to find Blue Healer Auctions || Drop us a line

Each spread and total pick carries a unit rating from 0 to 3 units. Jacksonville -10, the Rams -6 and Kansas City -1.5 get 2.5 units apiece. Still, receiver DJ Moore, tight end Dalton Kincaid and right tackle Spencer Brown are all questionable, which keeps the spread play small. Titans quarterback Cam Ward has one 200-yard passing game this season, and he’s without receiver Carnell Tate and running back Tyjae Spears, with receiver Calvin Ridley questionable. item.title: Milestones keep coming as Canandaigua volleyball chases a title
item.description: CANANDAIGUA – Maya Wiitanen and Addison Eckert were quick to identify what drives Canandaigua girls' volleyball. Fun. Energy. Positivity. Those traits, the senior captains said, define the group which is seeded first in the Section V Class A playoffs. They moved one step closer to the finals with a Halloween sweep of No. 8 Batavia (25-18, 25-14, 25-15). Canandaigua has lost just twice this season. It avenged its most recent setback – an Oct. 5 sweep to Pittsford Mendon – by defeating the Vikings three weeks later. Kadyn Chapman, a junior, reached 1,000 career assists against Batavia. She’s not the first Gray Wolves standout to reach a milestone this season. Eckert recorded her 500th career dig on Sept. 18. Wiitanen reached 1,000 career digs four days later. Watch above as the captains detail Canandaigua’s win over Batavia, its eight-game winning streak, and the mindset driving its Section V run. Jeff Uveino joined the USA Today Network in 2023 and began covering Rochester-area high school sports in 2026. He is a graduate of St. Bonaventure University's Jandoli School of Communication and native of Perry. Contact him at juveino@usatodayco.com . item.title: China follows through on threat as Real Madrid vs Racing Santander match removed from television schedule
item.description: China follows through on threat as Real Madrid vs Racing Santander match removed from television schedule Real Madrid and Kylian Mbappe have found themselves embroiled in an unnecessary controversy with China. The Frenchman’s remarks in an interview are now directly affecting the club’s television exposure , and there seems to be no resolution in sight. Despite formal apologies from both the player and the club, it looks as though China Media Group have no intention of budging. According to El Partidazo de COPE , Chinese television will not broadcast Los Blancos ‘ encounter against Racing Santander on Sunday. The large-scale boycott announced following Mbappe’s controversial comments seemingly remains in place. Real Madrid and La Liga disappear from Chinese television The dispute began after Mbappe discussed a meme depicting him as former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. His remarks triggered considerable criticism in China, prompting state broadcaster CCTV to suspend its coverage of La Liga . The consequences have extended beyond Real Madrid. CCTV did not broadcast any Spanish league matches on Friday or Saturday. Even Barcelona’s 6-1 victory over Deportivo Alaves was not broadcast in the Asian country. Meanwhile, Chinese streaming platform Migu took a different stance. The platform, which holds exclusive digital rights to La Liga until 2030, continued showing other league fixtures but removed Sunday’s Racing Santander-Real Madrid encounter. Apologies have failed to restore broadcasts Mbappe has already apologised publicly, while Real Madrid and La Liga have also attempted to repair relations with Chinese authorities. Nevertheless, the broadcasting restrictions remain unresolved, with no official indication of when normal coverage might resume. The concern for La Liga is that China represents an important international market, and sustained restrictions would affect both the club’s and the league’s revenue. Kylian Mbappe finds himself neck deep in an unnecessary controversy. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) The situation is particularly frustrating because Madrid have already made efforts to address the controversy. However, so far, Chinese authorities have deemed the efforts made by the player and the club insufficient and are showing no signs of backing down. Real Madrid cannot let this situation affect them on the pitch. The priority has to be to take three points at El Sardinero , and it remains to be seen how this controversy is resolved.

item.title: Is Saquon Barkley playing today? Injury update, start-or-sit advice for Week 8
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles will look to get back on track when they face the Washington Commanders in NFL Week 8. Sitting at 2-5, they cannot afford many more setbacks as they try to turn things around. Saquon Barkley is one player whose availability has drawn attention ahead of Sunday’s divisional matchup. The running back returned from a two-game absence last week but struggled to stay on the field throughout the contest. The Eagles have since provided another update on Barkley’s availability. Here’s what to know about his status and what fantasy managers should expect. MORE: Week 8 sell-high trade targets: Goff, Pollard, Pitts fantasy inflated Is Saquon Barkley playing today? Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Yes, Barkley is expected to play against the Commanders on Sunday night. The Eagles cleared the running back by leaving him off their final injury report on Friday. Barkley missed Wednesday and Thursday’s practices with hamstring and back injuries before returning as a limited participant on Friday. His return was an encouraging sign after he dealt with both issues during last week’s loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Friday's Injury Report #PHIvsWAS pic.twitter.com/FWs60KQd2c — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 30, 2026 Barkley managed just 10 snaps against the Cowboys but still finished with 71 scrimmage yards and a touchdown. His limited involvement raises questions about how much work he can handle against Washington. The running back said after Friday’s practice that he felt good enough to return, while also stressing the importance of listening to the medical staff and being smart with his recovery. Should you start Saquon Barkley in fantasy football? Fantasy managers can consider starting Barkley against Washington, but they should be cautious about expecting his usual workload. His availability is encouraging, but last week’s performance showed how much his injuries can affect his playing time. His touchdown helped rescue his fantasy performance last week, but relying on another score would be risky. Managers with reliable alternatives at running back should weigh those options before locking Barkley into their lineups. Verdict: Start Barkley if you do not have a stronger option. His health and potential workload make him a less dependable fantasy option this week. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Fifa Laopakdee joins Hideki Matsuyama with back-to-back Asia-Pacific Amateur victories
item.description: Fifa Laopakdee refused to listen to the voices inside his head. The senior at Arizona State has not played his best golf over the past year. About a year ago, he won the biggest championship of his life, claiming the Asia-Pacific Amateur. Since then, his game has been bogged down and his mind clouded with bad thoughts and impatience. He didn't let that stop him from joining an exclusive club Sunday. Laopakdee won the 2026 Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship at Te Arai Links in New Zealand, coming from behind in the final round to defeat Zack Swanwick by three shots. Laopakdee joins Hideki Matsuyama as the only players to win consecutive AAC titles, and that made his latest victory even more special. "I feel like I'm more proud of myself this year because I never stopped believing in myself, and even though I have a tough year," Laopakdee said. "I literally didn't win a single thing since March. I just keep telling myself that I've still got it. There was a demon in my said that said I don't have it anymore but there was still a big part of me that still believes in myself. "This win means a lot because I'm able to prove to myself that I've still got it." The moment Fifa Laopakdee secured the 2026 Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship for a second time. 🙌 #AACGolf pic.twitter.com/UKH0T2BP7a — Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship (@AAC_Golf) November 1, 2026 Laopakdee, who opened in 63 on Thursday and closed with a 1-under 70 on Sunday, was in chase mode until the 11th hole. Swanwick carded a triple bogey 7 while Laopakdee made a birdie for a four-shot swing. He went from chasing to leading with only seven holes to go, saying he felt his hands shaking on the birdie putt. But his mentality didn't change. He wanted to still believe he was chasing. It just wasn't another person; it was history. With the win, Laopakdee will return to the Masters and Open Championship in 2027 after competing in both majors for the first time earlier this year. Both experiences helped show him what life after college was going to be like. "You share the same locker room, share the same dining hall, share the same practice round, you get to experience how those people live," Laopakdee said. "I just learned from it and it made me a lot more mature, and I've started to read books now that help with my brain now. I love reading about golf psychology, like the Bob Rotella book. "This morning, the whole week, when I have a late tee time, I wake up, eat breakfast, go back to my room, read books, write down notes in my journal and try to find something that I can use on the course, and it worked out perfectly." Now the history books will have to include him in the same conversations as Matsuyama when discussing the AAC. Laopakdee hasn't met the 2021 Masters champion yet, but perhaps that will change next April at Augusta National. "Hideki has played a huge part in golf for Japan, and also Asia," Laopakdee said. "Being able to win back-to-back like him is a huge honor. He's a great player

item.title: Why one Indiana Hoosiers star reminds Jason Whitlock of Fernando Mendoza
item.description: Photo by CFP/Getty Images Fernando Mendoza’s influence on the Indiana Hoosiers is still around, and Jason Whitlock recently took notice of it. The Indiana Hoosiers won their first ever NCAA Division I Football championship in 2025-26, powered by star quarterback Fernando Mendoza. This led to the 23-year-old becoming the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, being picked up by the Las Vegas Raiders. The Heisman Trophy winner left quite the impact on his team. Outside of the success he led them to, his faith has apparently been something that has left its mark. Following recent comments from his former teammate Charlie Becker, Jason Whitlock has commented on it. Jason Whitlock hailed Charlie Becker’s ‘awesome testimony’ following his big performance While Mendoza is in the big leagues now, Becker is still playing for the Hoosiers. In their latest win against the Minnesota Golden Gophers, he had a monster game. The youngster had eight receptions for 149 yards and one touchdown. Following the game, his interview was heavily influenced by his Christian faith. He declared that the ‘God he serves’ is amazing and remarkable, and was very open about his devout beliefs. This has impressed Whitlock, who shouted him out after the game. “Charlie Becker. Awesome testimony. He sounds like Fernando Mendoza,” Whitlock wrote on X, seemingly having watched the interview. Becker and Mendoza became close friends and roommates at Indiana, with Becker living alongside the Raiders star and his brother Alberto. The receiver has compared them to family, talking about how Fernando’s work ethic, faith and preparation helped shape who he is today. It’s no wonder that Whitlock was reminded of the quarterback. item.title: MSU volleyball pushes No. 1 Nebraska but falls, one day after heartbreaker against No. 19 Indiana
item.description: A day after a difficult five-set loss to a ranked opponent, Michigan State’s volleyball team made a statement early against No. 1 Nebraska at Breslin Center on Saturday, with the Spartans playing two of their better sets of the season before falling in four sets, 21-25, 25-19, 25-17, 25-12. No. 25 MSU’s losses to Indiana and the Huskers over the weekend drop the Spartans to 17-5 overall and 7-5 in the Big Ten. Saturday’s game was played in front of more than 8,000 fans, there to see MSU and the road show that is the top-ranked Huskers. “(Friday) night (against Indiana) was such a heartbreaker,” MSU coach Kristen Kelsay said. “And I’m so proud of our team to do the work — to do the work emotionally, to do the work with their mindset, to do the work with their bodies — to be able to come in and have the first two sets that we had. Not thrilled that we weren’t able to maintain that. There’s a reason that Nebraska is the best defensive team in the country. Hard-pressed to kill the ball. But from our serving pressure, from our blocking ability against these guys, there’s a lot of good to take from this.” Senior Alanna Bankston led MSU in kills with 12, while senior Zora Hardison added eight and four total blocks, with junior Breccan Scheck and freshman Madi Andrews adding five kills each. Scheck also hit .571 for the match and led MSU in total blocks with a team-best seven. Redshirt sophomore setter Malayah Long posted her fourth double-double of the season with team highs in both assists (26) and digs (10). Scheck’s performance was especially notable against Nebraska, because it came in place of Carmen Waye, who was injured in Friday’s loss to the Hoosiers, a match in which the Spartans took a two-set lead, before falling 19-25, 15-25, 25-19, 25-19, 15-7. Kelsay didn’t want to accept any moral victories, but was clearly pleased with her team’s grit Saturday. “What I learned is our team is tough — a reverse sweep and a critical injury to one of our star players (against Indiana), and then we come out and play the way we did in those first couple sets. Man, there’s a lot to like and a lot to take from that.” Next, MSU plays at No. 8 Wisconsin on Thursday. That match (which begins at 8 p.m. ET) can be streamed on Big Ten Network-plus. This article originally appeared on Lansing State Journal: MSU volleyball pushes No. 1 Nebraska but falls, one day after heartbreaker against No. 19 Indiana

item.title: Pitt puts away Georgia Tech, ends losing streak
item.description: FILE PHOTO - A new look University of Pittsburgh football helmet is on a table at Heinz Field during their annual intrasquad Blue-Gold spring NCAA football game, Saturday, April 13, 2019, in Pittsburgh. The Blue team won 14-7. (AP Photo/Keith Srakocic) Keith Srakocic This article originally appeared on PittsburghSportsNOW . Pitt is back on track. With a 34-11 win over Georgia Tech at home on Saturday night, Pat Narduzzi ‘s Panthers ended a three-game skid. True freshman tailback Damon Ferguson Jr. was the star of the night, punching it in twice and piling up 185 yards on 31 carries while his side’s defense quieted the visitors. To start things out, though, Pitt settled for a field goal after a rash of penalties on their second drive of the night, which began on Georgia Tech’s 31-yard line after the Yellow Jackets were pinned inside their 5 by Gabe Russo . One of those infractions, drawn by Ryan Carretta getting a paw in Tawfiq Thomas’ face, canceled out a 28-yard touchdown pass from fifth-year Holden Geriner to Malik Knight . Three plays later, Antonio Chadha nailed a 45-yard field goal. Click here to find depth charts and more on PittsburghSportsNOW. Download the FREE WPXI News app for breaking news alerts. item.title: Irish Olympian and European champion Ciara Mageean dies aged 34
item.description: Ireland ’s European 1500 metres gold medallist Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34 after suffering from cancer. Two-time Olympian Mageean, who won the European title in Rome in 2024, announced last year she had been diagnosed with cancer. A statement on her Instagram account on Sunday read: “At 6:30am this morning, Ciara lost her battle with cancer surrounded by her loved ones. A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed.” A statement from Athletics Ireland read: “Athletics Ireland is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Ciara Mageean. “Ciara was a much-loved and inspirational figure who touched the lives of so many. Her courage, warmth and spirit will leave a lasting legacy. “The thoughts and heartfelt condolences of everyone at Athletics Ireland are with Ciara’s family, friends and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time. “May she rest in peace.” f reland's Ciara Mageean celebrates with her bronze medal on the podium after finishing third in the Women's 1500m Final (PA) The athlete was from Portaferry, Co Down, Ireland. In a post on social media, her family said she was surrounded by her loved ones. They said: “A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed.” Tánaiste Simon Harris described the news as heartbreaking. He said on X: “She was a European champion, two-time Olympian, a proud Irish athlete and an extraordinary person.” Northern Ireland’s First Minister Michelle O’Neill said Mageean demonstrated “extraordinary talent, determination and dedication”. “I am deeply saddened to hear of the passing of Ciara Mageean, and I want to extend my heartfelt condolences to her husband Tommy, her parents, family, friends and everyone who loved her,” she said. “Ciara’s achievements in athletics brought immense pride to her local community and to people right across Ireland. “From representing Ireland at two Olympic Games to winning European Championship gold in Rome in 2024, Ciara demonstrated extraordinary talent, determination and dedication. “However, beyond the medals, records and sporting accolades, Ciara will be remembered for her warmth, courage and tremendous strength of character. “Throughout her illness, she showed a remarkable spirit and an incredible ability to find hope and joy in life, even in the most difficult circumstances. Her courage touched countless people and will leave a lasting legacy. “For a community like Portaferry, this loss will be deeply felt. Ciara was one of our own, and the pride she brought to her community and beyond will never be forgotten. “At this incredibly difficult time, I hope her family and loved ones can take some comfort from knowing just how deeply she was admired, respected and loved by so many people.” Deputy First Minister Emma Little-Pengelly said: “I am so sorry to hear of the death of Ciara Mageean, at the age of 34 years. “An outstanding athlete and ambassador for her sport, Ciara was bo

item.title: Ireland 'optimistic' on Prendergast fitness
item.description: Prendergast has earned 17 Ireland caps [Getty Images] Ireland are optimistic that Sam Prendergast will be fit for Friday's Nations Championship opener against Argentina as the fly-half continues his recovery from a wrist injury. Prendergast, 23, missed Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster on 24 October after injuring his wrist in training. Speaking after that game, Leinster head coach Leo Cullen admitted Prendergast recovering in time to face the Pumas would be "tight". But in a squad update issued on Sunday, the Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) said he "continues to improve" and that "management are optimistic" he will be available for selection. Ireland head coach Andy Farrell is already without the injured Jack Crowley, with Connacht's Ciaran Frawley and uncapped Ulster player Jamie Benson the other options at fly-half. In positive news, Leinster utility back Jimmy O'Brien will be available to face Argentina. The 29-year-old has resumed training having passed return to play protocols after sustaining a concussion against Munster. Ireland host Argentina on Friday (20:10 GMT) before home matches with Fiji and South Africa on 14 and 21 November, and a finals weekend fixture against a yet-to-be determined southern hemisphere opponent the following week at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium. In the southern hemisphere leg of the Nations Championship in July, Ireland beat Australia and Japan before losing to New Zealand in Auckland.

item.title: Bayern's Saibari has surgery on ankle as Gnabry injures hamstring
item.description: Bayern Munich's Ismael Saibari is assisted after picking up an injury during the German Bundesliga soccer match between FC Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern's Saibari has surgery on ankle as Gnabry injures hamstring») Sven Hoppe/dpa Bayern Munich forward Ismael Saibari has already had an operation on an ankle injury sustained in Saturday's 2-2 Bundesliga draw at home to Borussia Dortmund, while Serge Gnabry has been diagnosed with a hamstring problem. The injury-hit German champions issued a health update on Sunday after more players were sidelined along with Manuel Neuer, Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz. "Saibari tore the syndesmotic ligament in his right ankle and has already had surgery. Gnabry sustained a muscular injury in his left hamstring," Bayern said without giving a timeline on when the pair might return. There was no mention of Michael Olise, who limped off late on against Dortmund. Bayern added that the operation for Morocco's Saibari, a big transfer window addition, had been successful. Winger Gnabry, 31, was only back fit after missing Germany's ill-fated World Cup tilt due an adductor injury. The champions' problems, which include coach Vincent Kompany so far missing three games with illness, are putting a huge strain on their squad. Three recognized left backs were on the pitch during the second half against Dortmund. Bayern, who have previously said they are not interested in January signings, go to Atlético Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday.

item.title: Lorenzo Musetti Shows What It Takes To Win a Trophy in Tennis
item.description: Aug 21, 2026; Mason, OH, USA; Lorenzo Musetti (ITA) returns a shot against Frances Tiafoe (USA) during the Cincinnati Open at Lindner Family Tennis Center. Mandatory Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Steen Kirby If you’re wondering about what it takes to win a trophy in tennis these days, Lorenzo Musetti showed us . Apparently, you have to play until one in the morning, spend three and a half hours chasing tennis balls around an indoor court, survive four match points the following afternoon, and somehow find enough energy to beat one of the world’s best players in the final. At least, that is what Lorenzo Musetti had to do. The Italian won the ATP 250 title in Lyon on Sunday , defeating Taylor Fritz 6-3 6-4 to claim his third career trophy and first since October 2022. Four years without a title and seven consecutive defeats in finals, and after everything he endured in France, the championship match turned out to be the easiest part of the week. Musetti Shows What It Takes To Win a Trophy in Tennis Three and a Half Hours, and That Was Just Friday Musetti’s tournament began innocently enough: he defeated Matteo Arnaldi 6-1 6-4 in the opening round, then followed with a 6-4 6-4 win over Moise Kouame. Nothing special in those two, but then came Luca Van Assche. The Frenchman and Musetti produced one of the season’s most ridiculous indoor matches, spending three hours and 32 minutes exchanging increasingly exhausting baseline rallies on Lyon’s painfully slow court. Neither had the power to consistently hit through the other, and both are exceptional movers, which made things worse. In the end, the result was an apparently endless sequence of points that should have finished several shots earlier. Musetti eventually won 7-6 6-7 6-4 as the match finished at 1:17 a.m. local time, just six minutes short of the famous three-hour, 38-minute Murray-Raonic encounter at the 2016 ATP Finals. And what was Musetti’s reward? A semi-final against world No. 6 Flavio Cobolli the following afternoon. Wonderful. Four Match Points, Then Somehow a Trophy Cobolli, who had enjoyed considerably more time to recover, was hardly interested in making life easy for his compatriot, and he showed it by winning the opening set 6-4. Musetti then responded by taking the second 6-2, but the deciding set produced another extraordinary ordeal. At 5-4, Cobolli earned four match points on Musetti’s serve and, true to the ridiculous fashion his week had taken up to that point, Musetti saved every single one. Then, as if recovering from the brink of defeat wasn’t enough, he broke Cobolli in the next game and served out the match 4-6 6-2 7-5. Another two and a half hours on court, and consider what that meant. In roughly 24 hours, Musetti had spent more than six hours competing, finished one match after 1 a.m. and saved four match points against a Top 10 opponent. He was now expected to recover and face Fritz in Sunday’s final. And this was a player who h

item.title: The NYC Marathon Has A Net Zero Goal. Can Global Sports Keep Pace?
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 02: Competitors cross the finish line during the 2025 TCS New York City Marathon on November 02, 2025 in New York City. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) Getty Images As the NYC Marathon marks 50 years across five boroughs, organizers test how athletes, sponsors, and cities can cut event emissions. Today, more than 50,000 runners are expected to take to the streets of New York City for the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon, crossing five boroughs as millions of spectators cheer them on. For many athletes, completing the 26.2-mile course represents a lifetime achievement. For New York, the race is an international sporting tradition. But bringing so many people together also presents a substantial environmental challenge. This year’s marathon marks the 50th anniversary of its five-borough course, introduced in 1976. New York Road Runners (NYRR), the nonprofit organization behind the event, is considering what it will take to make the race more sustainable over the next half-century. The answer involves more than recyclable water bottles, electric vehicles or collecting discarded clothing. It requires rethinking how major sporting events operate, how corporate partners contribute to environmental goals and how host cities benefit after the crowds disappear. “The TCS New York City Marathon’s biggest source of emissions is travel to New York City,” said Aly Criscuolo, NYRR’s director of sustainability and corporate social responsibility, in a written interview. That finding illustrates the central environmental paradox facing international sporting events. Their success depends partly on attracting participants from around the world, but the transportation required to bring those participants together contributes to climate change. For NYRR, the challenge is particularly relevant as the organization works toward its goal of achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2040. The climate challenge behind the finish line The environmental impact of major sporting events extends well beyond the venues where athletes compete. Transportation, energy consumption, waste disposal, equipment manufacturing and supply chains all contribute to an event’s environmental footprint. According to the International Academy of Sport Science and Technology , sustainable sporting events require integrated management strategies that consider environmental, economic, and social consequences throughout the planning and delivery process. International frameworks such as ISO 20121, which addresses sustainability management for events, emphasize planning, accountability and measurable performance. These principles are increasingly relevant as sporting organizations face expectations to demonstrate environmental progress rather than simply announce sustainability commitments. item.title: Changing of the guard? Aaron Danks comments on Bayern Munich’s center-back depth chart
item.description: (Photo by S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Minjae Kim has featured in all Champions League fixtures for Bayern Munich this season along with Dayot Upamecano. In the Der Klassiker fixture in the Bundesliga, the same pairing started the game. Assistant coach Aaron Danks was asked whether Kim has pipped Jonathan Tah to become Upa’s primary partner in defense this season. “We’ve got three top center-backs. I thought the two that played today, Kim and Upamecano, put in a fantastic performance. I thought they had some really, really good moments. And Jonathan Tah also had put in two very good performances recently, so we’re blessed with really good players. And they all take their moments to perform for us,” answered Danks (as captured by @iMiaSanMia) . Standing in for the recovering Vincent Kompany, Danks is temporarily in charge of the Bayern Munich senior team. He set up the backline with Upa and Kim as the central defenders, with Alphonso Davies and Konrad Laimer completing the defense as the left-back and right-back, respectively. Kim led the backline with a game-high 13 defensive contributions, including seven clearances, killing off dangerous runs by the lethal Dortmund side. Tah and Kim vary in their profiles as defenders. Kim brings a dimension of raw physical dominance and unrelenting drive in tackles. Tah, on the other hand, is composed and calculated, maintaining constant communication with his teammates. Hiroki Ito has struggled to build rhythm despite having moments of absolute brilliance in both defense and build-up. However, one defender Bayern are missing is a young talent who can be the backup defender and learn the ropes from these experienced seniors. Join the conversation! item.title: Jack Nicklaus once revealed his honest opinion on Brooks Koepka as a golfer
item.description: Photo by Ben Jared/PGA TOUR via Getty Images Jack Nicklaus has won everything there is to win in the game. Nicklaus racked up 73 PGA Tour wins throughout his illustrious career, including a record 18 major championships. Meanwhile, Koepka only has nine PGA Tour wins to his name, but five of those have been majors. He is definitely a player who excels when the pressure is at its most intense, and his record in the majors proves that. Brooks Koepka has a mentality that few golfers possess whereby he is more comfortable when challenging for majors down the back nine than he is playing in a regular PGA Tour event. Jack Nicklaus was the same. The Golden Bear often produced his best golf when he needed it most in the four biggest tournaments in the sport. So, it surely goes without saying that the now 86-year-old will have great respect for someone who performs similarly to the way that he did during his prime. Jack Nicklaus shared his opinion on Brooks Koepka as a golfer During an interview with the Palm Beach Post , Nicklaus gave his true feelings on Koepka as a player, just after he won his second US Open title in a row at Shinnecock Hills in 2018. “I like him,” Nicklaus said. “He’s a strong kid. As I said at the Open he was calm, collected and confident. You could add cool to that if you want to. “Once you win one U.S. Open and then you come back and win another U.S. Open, all of a sudden you believe that you can do what you’re doing. You believe in your own stuff. “It looked like he believed he was in his rightful place. He played like it. He did a great job. I was very happy for him, very proud of him. I was delighted to see how well he played.” Of course, Koepka went on to win three more majors after his victory at Shinnecock Hills in 2018. All three of those majors came at the PGA Championship in 2018, 2019 and 2023. Now the 36-year-old will be intent on adding to his major tally as he attempts to write his name in the history books as one of the greatest to ever do it.

item.title: Mets Castoff Tyler Zuber Cut By Division Rival Shortly After Brutal Injury Setback
item.description: ANAHEIM, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 2: A detail view of a New York Mets logo on a hat prior to a game against the Los Angeles Angels at Angel Stadium of Anaheim on August 2, 2024 in Anaheim, California. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) Getty Images The New York Mets have plenty of difficult decisions ahead as they attempt to regroup following another disappointing season. With questions surrounding the roster, potential free-agent additions and the possibility of significant changes before Opening Day, the coming weeks could prove pivotal for the franchise, all with the cloud of a looming labor lockout ahead. “With free agency set to begin soon, there’s every reason to believe there will be a spending frenzy over the next month with the lockout looming on Dec. 1 when the CBA expires,” Danny Abriano wrote for SNY . “So the Mets, and every other team, could be in a race to that theoretical deadline.” While New York prepares for that potentially chaotic stretch, the organization received an update on a former pitcher castoff who recently found himself on the wrong side of a significant roster decision by a National League East division rival. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets, Yankees Castoff Clay Holmes Cuts Ties With Cubs After Very Short Stint New York Mets Castoff Outrighted By Division Rival After Elbow Surgery Former Mets right-hander Tyler Zuber has been outrighted by the Miami Marlins, shortly after suffering an injury that could cost him the entire 2027 campaign. “Marlins sent RHP Tyler Zuber, RHP Zach Brzykcy, RHP Wikelman Gonzalez, C Brian Navarreto and C Logan Driscoll outright to Triple-A Jacksonville,” Matthew Pouliot reported for NBC Sports . “Zuber recently underwent internal brace surgery that could keep him out for all of next year.” The decision represents another setback for Zuber, who had been working to establish himself as a reliable major-league relief option. The 31-year-old previously spent time with the Kansas City Royals and Tampa Bay Rays before making his way to Queens for a brief stint last year. The Rays traded him to the Mets in July 2024 and he made just one major-league appearance for New York before being placed on waivers and moving on to Miami. item.title: Club beyond saving? Baumgart lays into German side
item.description: Club beyond saving? Baumgart lays into German side Following his sacking by Union Berlin, Steffen Baumgart is currently without a club. Asked whether he could see himself taking charge at struggling Hannover 96, the 54-year-old made his feelings more than clear. “Look, Hannover, no offence: Who can save Hannover? Who can pull that off? How long have things not been working there?” Baumgart asked rhetorically in an interview with 'Bild', before stressing that he would not back himself to do it. Strong words from the former Union coach, who is usually so self-confident. Hannover only dismissed sporting director Jonas Boldt yesterday, and head coach Sandro Wagner is already on the brink after just a few weeks in charge. Hannover are hosting Dynamo Dresden right now, with Wagner’s future likely also at stake. Will Baumgart reconsider his comments if Wagner has to go after today’s game? item.description: Tompolo donates 30 campaign vehicles, launches 10,000 canvassers By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The re-election campaign of President Bola Tinubu in Osun State received a boost at the weekend as Governor Ademola Adeleke and his predecessor, Adegboyega Oyetola, pledged to work together to secure victory for the President in the 2027 election. The commitment came as the Grand Patron of the President Bola Tinubu Door-to-Door Movement, High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, launched 10,000 canvassers and donated 30 campaign vehicles and public address systems to support the mobilisation drive. Speaking at the launch held at Freedom Park, Osogbo, representatives of Adeleke and Oyetola called on political leaders and stakeholders to set aside their differences and work towards delivering the targeted 1.5 million votes for Tinubu in the state. Oyetola, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, who was represented by Bola Oyebamiji, urged the canvassers to approach the assignment with sincerity, discipline and commitment. He cautioned them against hypocrisy, political pretence and complacency, while appealing to political leaders, interest groups and other stakeholders to put aside personal interests and differences. “I appeal to all political leaders, interest groups, individuals and stakeholders to rise above selfish interests, personal ego and political differences. Let us demonstrate that political differences need not prevent us from pursuing a shared national objective. “With unity of purpose, effective grassroots mobilisation and unwavering commitment, we can deliver the 1.5 million votes targeted for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Osun State and secure victory for our party’s candidates at all levels,” he said. In his remarks, Adeleke, who is the state coordinator of the Presidential Campaign Council and was represented by his deputy, Kola Adewusi, described the launch of the canvassers and donation of vehicles as timely for the commencement of the President’s campaign in the state. He urged coalition partners to put aside past disagreements and work together, saying the partnership was focused primarily on the presidential election. “Our gathering is therefore a timely push to gain further momentum in the campaign process. We must therefore forget past disagreements and unite to deliver for the President. “All coalition partners have a duty to overlook all previous relationship antagonism and join hands to deliver between 1.5 to 2 million votes for Mr President,” he said. item.title: My challenge to the Bills against Ravens in Week 8
item.description: I’m challenging the Buffalo Bills to do something specific in this Week 8 game against Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens. How about a truly convincing win over a quality opponent? Maybe even a wire-to-wire victory. No comeback needed. Heck, let’s even up it to a two-score margin. Parity has never been more ubiquitous in this game, which is largely why the NFL is so damn good and endlessly entertaining. A win is a win in this league, but I can’t write that all wins are viewed as equal. And existing solely in one-score game land is living dangerously. Over time, essentially all clubs regress to the mean in those tight contests. Now, teams with superstar quarterbacks and a collection of other excellent players can stay on the right side of the ledger in the hard-fought battles, but it’s not how any organization wants to regularly operate. And, right now, even at 5-1, just for their reputation and perceived staying power, the Bills are dire need of a game in which they were, undeniably, the better team throughout. It’s been a while for the Bills to secure that type of a win against a legitimately strong opponent. Since the beginning of 2020, Buffalo owns the league’s best collective point differential… by an enormous margin. They’ve outscored their combined opponents by 902 points. The Ravens have the second-best point differential in that time frame… at +581 points. That’s almost unfathomable, isn’t it? A season ago, the Bills beat the eventual 10-7 Steelers 26-7 in Pittsburgh, a thoroughly dominant, run-game driven thrashing of an eventual above .500 playoff team. That game felt out of reach for the Steelers for the vast majority of the contest. Obviously though, that Pittsburgh team was thoroughly flawed despite the regular-season record it managed. In the 2024-2025 wild-card round, the Bills beat an upstart 10-7 Broncos team with rookie quarterback Bo Nix 31-7 at home. Earlier that year, Josh Allen’s thunderous fourth-down scamper late against the, at the time, undefeated Kansas City Chiefs that finished 15-2, catapulted the Bills to a nine-point victory. But even that game got dicey late, of course. And it was Allen’s heroics that lifted Buffalo to a two-score win. A few weeks prior to that, Allen and Co. commanded the game from start to finish in Seattle against the eventual 10-7 Seahawks in a 31-10 win. What I’ve listed above are the Bills’ only triumphs by more than a touchdown over teams that finished above .500 in the past two seasons. And yes, blowout wins over eventual playoff teams are, quite naturally, reasonably rare for every club in the modern NFL. The ability to win close games is what separates the bad from the good and the good from the great. But Buffalo is past destroying bad-to-average teams. We know the Bills can do those things. They’ve been decidedly better at it than anyone else in football in the post-2020 Allen era. This core mission of this team is beating good teams in January and February, and while they’ll have t

item.title: 'Mother of all editors' Emacs is 50
item.description: No lesser authority than the MIT Technology Review says that the Emacs editor has turned 50 years old. But then, it is biased — Emacs was invented in MIT's AI lab. Simson Garfinkel's article is simply called EMACS turns 50, but the sub-heading explains why it matters more: "How the MIT AI Lab's text editor gave birth to the free software movement." There are multiple timelines and accounts of the origins of Emacs, and it is not a single monolithic application. The name is an abbreviation for " E diting MAC ro S ", and the original editor for which this set of macros was developed was TECO – "Text Editor and COrrector," written by Dan Murphy in 1962. Murphy died earlier this year at the age of 83. The inimitable Jamie Zawinski has an encyclopedic Emacs Timeline – as he mentions at the start, his interest being that he long ago maintained a fork of GNU Emacs, originally called Lucid Emacs . It's still around, under its later name XEmacs. There are a lot of forks and re-implementations of Emacs out there, and we are not going to go into all of them, or this article would become a book – one only interesting to programmer-archeologists (to use a term coined by the late great Vernor Vinge ). As for who originally wrote those Editing Macros, though, another history has quotations from several of the people involved: On the Origin of Emacs in 1976 . (Note – some of the quotes still contain the | symbols that marked quoted text.) This credits Lisp boffin Guy L. Steele Jr with the original work in 1975, but in it, Steele says: "RMS is responsible for the names 'E' and 'EMACS'. RMS still deserves 99% or 99.9% or 99.99% or 99.999% of the credit for taking a package of TECO macros and turning it into the most powerful editor on the planet." RMS is of course Richard Stallman, and the page also quotes some emails from RMS on October 23 and 31, 1976. Mind you, just a few years after the event, in a 1981 talk now preserved on the GNU website, Stallman said, "I began the development of EMACS in 1974 with an improvement to TECO". Like all the best FOSS, even in its very early stages, it was a collaborative effort – but around late October 1976 is when RMS took over the bulk of the development. Of the many forks of Emacs over its half a century of development, some are still just about hanging on in there. When we looked up the link for XEmacs, we were surprised to see that there was a new release: XEmacs 21.5.37 "lettuce" appeared just last month. And even the forks have forks: in this case, SXEmacs , last updated in 2020. Most of the changes in XEmacs and SXEmacs eventually made their way back upstream to GNU Emacs, which is still in active development, although as The Register reported in 2008 , RMS is no longer the primary maintainer. GNU Emacs 31.1 appeared in August. Cards on the metaphorical table: this vulture is not an Emacs user. We have tried. item.title: Osun group demands arrest of Sowore’s attackers
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo A coalition of civil society organisations in Osun State, The Osun Masterminds (TOM), has condemned the reported attack on the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Mr Omoyele Sowore, in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State, and called on security agencies to identify and prosecute those responsible. The group described the incident as a national disgrace and an assault on Nigerians’ rights to participate in politics, express their views and support candidates of their choice. TOM’s Executive Director, Professor Wasiu Oyedokun-Alli, made the position known during the group’s monthly briefing on the state of the nation. He said elections should provide an opportunity for candidates and political parties to present their policies and development plans to the electorate, rather than become occasions for violence and intimidation. “Elections should be a festival of ideas, a peaceful contest of developmental blueprints, and a developmental milestone where the sovereign will of the people is freely expressed,” he said. Oyedokun-Alli called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant agencies to investigate the reported attack and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. “We call on the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services (DSS), and all relevant statutory agencies to rise above partisan politics and uphold the rule of law,” he said. The group expressed concern that the political environment was becoming increasingly hostile to opposition figures and Nigerians expressing dissenting views. It alleged that the electoral space was being turned into a combat zone where opposition figures and dissenting voices were targeted, silenced and physically assaulted. Describing the reported attack as a national disgrace, particularly because it allegedly occurred in a public space, TOM also criticised what it said were attempts by security agencies and law enforcement authorities to downplay attacks on political figures. “When security apparatuses and law enforcement agencies trivialize such high-profile acts of violence—dismissing life-threatening injuries as ‘minor’ or engaging in administrative denials—they surrender their neutrality and embolden the forces of tyranny,” the group stated. Oyedokun-Alli warned that Nigeria could not guarantee credible, free and fair elections in 2027 if political violence was allowed to prevent candidates from campaigning and engaging with voters. The post Osun group demands arrest of Sowore’s attackers appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Lagos begins joint enforcement of badges for Danfo operators
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The Lagos State Government has announced plans to commence joint enforcement of compulsory identification badges and other regulatory requirements for commercial bus operators, popularly known as Danfo drivers and conductors, to strengthen commuter safety and accountability. The enforcement drive, being coordinated by the State Ministry of Transportation through its Directorate of Public Transport and Commuter Services (PTCS), will involve the Vehicle Inspection Service (VIS) and the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA). The Director of Public Transport and Commuter Services, Mr Nuhman Edu, said the initiative was designed to improve commuter security, ensure accountability among transport operators and strengthen compliance with established transport regulations. He identified some of the major compliance gaps the exercise would address to include improper commuter vehicle registration, absence of vehicle body tags, stage carriage permits, drivers’ badges and conductors’ badges. Edu explained that the collaboration with VIS and LASTMA would strengthen the verification of relevant safety documents during routine enforcement operations. “Where a vehicle is found to be non-compliant, enforcement or compliance procedures will be initiated strictly in accordance with extant laws, regulations, approved guidelines and established operational procedures,” he said. He said proper identification of commercial vehicles, drivers and conductors would make operators traceable, improve accountability, assist investigations involving vehicles allegedly used in criminal activities and facilitate the prompt resolution of commuter complaints. According to him, the framework will clearly define the responsibilities of the participating agencies across six areas. These include verification of prescribed PTCS documents, recording of vehicle compliance status, identification of violations, initiation of enforcement or corrective measures, information exchange and data-sharing, as well as referral of cases requiring further administrative or regulatory action. Edu said commuter safety and security remained the primary reasons for strengthening regulation of public transportation in the state. He added that the ministry would engage transport unions and associations through stakeholder meetings, media campaigns and sensitisation programmes to ensure operators understood the requirements. The director further disclosed that the ministry had resolved to introduce continuous monitoring, evaluation and assessment of compliance levels across the state, supported by reporting and feedback mechanisms to ensure timely identification and resolution of regulatory gaps. The post Lagos begins joint enforcement of badges for Danfo operators appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘It was a prayer walk’ – Pastor Adeboye denies carrying placard against Jonathan
item.description: The General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Enoch Adeboye, has faulted media reports regarding a placard he carried during a prayer walk under former President Goodluck Jonathan’s administration. The cleric spoke on Sunday during the church’s November Thanksgiving service, where he accused a journalist of misrepresenting the incident and portraying him as a wicked person for allegedly carrying a placard against the former president. Recounting how he came across the report, Adeboye said he was initially amused by the claim. “Recently, somebody wrote in the papers, or said somehow, ‘Pastor Adeboye is a very wicked man. After all, we know that not too long ago, he carried a placard against President Goodluck Jonathan,’” he said. While admitting that he carried a placard, the cleric insisted that the exercise was a prayer walk and not a protest against Jonathan. “True, I carried a placard. I can’t deny that. It was important. It was a prayer walk. We wanted to pray,” he said. He explained that the exercise followed a directive asking churches to organise prayer walks around their premises. “The chairman said all churches should do a prayer walk near their churches. That’s what I did,” he said. Adeboye further argued that the date of the exercise contradicted the report’s suggestion that he carried the placard against Jonathan while he was president. “But I carried the placard in 2020. Jonathan ceased to be president in 2015. I carried the placard five years in the second term of Buhari,” Adeboye said. He accused the journalist of distorting the facts and criticised the failure to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident before publishing the report. “But a journalist twisted it. I said, I did what I did in 2015. And everybody swallowed it,” he said. The RCCG leader also recalled his exposure to journalism studies in the 1960s, saying he was taught the importance of investigative journalism and verifying information before publication. “I remember in those days in the Department of Journalism, when you go there and you take a course, they talked about something called investigative journalism,” he said. He added, “That things don’t appear as they may seem. Investigate, if you have a story, before you take it to the press.” Vanguard News The post ‘It was a prayer walk’ – Pastor Adeboye denies carrying placard against Jonathan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Vanguard, TVC, Channels, others fix November 8 for Lagos governorship debate
item.description: LAGOS — The Nigeria Debate Consortium has fixed November 8, 2026, for a governorship debate involving candidates contesting the 2027 Lagos State governorship election. The debate, scheduled for 7 p.m., will hold at The Hub by IALA, House of His Glory, Plot 18, Providence Road, beside Keystone Bank, Marwa, Lekki, Lagos. The consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, TheCable and Vanguard Newspaper, said the debate would kick-start its series of electoral engagements ahead of the 2027 general elections, covering selected battleground states before culminating in a presidential debate and town hall. In a statement announcing the event, the consortium said the initiative was designed to provide a credible, non-partisan platform for governorship candidates to present their agendas, defend their policy choices and respond to questions on issues affecting Lagos residents. It said the debate would focus on critical areas, including transportation, infrastructure, security, housing, education, healthcare, job creation and economic growth, allowing voters to assess the candidates’ proposals and readiness to govern. Channels Television said the initiative reflected the media’s responsibility to inform the electorate and strengthen democratic accountability. “Voters deserve more than campaign promises; they deserve clear answers, credible plans and an opportunity to assess those seeking their mandate,” the organisation said. It added that the debate would place issues, ideas and the future of Lagos at the centre of the electoral conversation, helping citizens make informed choices based on candidates’ proposals and their capacity to deliver. Similarly, TVC News described the debate as an opportunity for candidates to move beyond political rhetoric and demonstrate the substance of their vision for the state. “Citizens need to understand not only what candidates promise, but how they intend to deliver,” it said, adding that a fair platform for such engagement would promote accountability and an informed electorate. The consortium said the debate would be conducted in line with established professional standards, with fairness, neutrality, equal opportunity and editorial independence as guiding principles. It added that all participating candidates would be subjected to the same rules, speaking times and moderation standards. Experienced journalists are expected to moderate the debate, which will be broadcast to national and digital audiences through the participating media organisations’ platforms. The consortium called on Lagos residents, particularly eligible voters, young people, civil society organisations, professional groups and the business community, to follow the debate and engage with the issues and choices facing the state. The statement was jointly signed by Babajide Kolade-Otitoju, Director of News, TVC News, and Kingsley Uranta, General Manager, Channels Television. item.title: Germany ‘Gen Z Regelt’ Protest Turned Violent As Rioters Loot Shops
item.description: Masked rioters looted shops in the German city of Frankfurt on Saturday as massive demonstrations turned violent across the country, with police also firing water cannons at youths hurling Molotov cocktails. Several police officers were injured in the violence after tens of thousands joined youth-led protests across the country organised by the group “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!). The demonstrations, inspired by similar movements in France and Italy calling for political elites to heed the concerns of the younger generation, were largely peaceful during the day. But tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of young people refused to disperse, with violence breaking out in major cities including Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg. It was especially bad in the financial hub of Frankfurt, where police faced protesters hurling stones, fireworks and petrol bombs, and responded with water cannon and pepper spray. “Violent riots” were taking place, police said in a statement. “Windows have been smashed at several shops. Molotov cocktails are also being thrown at emergency personnel.” Protesters light flares after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” (Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP) A gun store was among the shops looted, with its windows smashed. Police said they arrested a suspect and seized two weapons. A trainer shop and a perfume store were also targeted, the Bild daily reported. A large section of Frankfurt’s main shopping street was closed off as authorities sought to quell the unrest, with police vans and riot police stopping anyone from entering, according to an AFP journalist. A police helicopter hovered overhead as sporadic blasts were heard on the street. At least one police officer was injured there and was receiving medical treatment. ‘Shameful’ Roman Poseck, interior minister of Hesse state, said that “around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists” had infiltrated the protest in Frankfurt. “It is shameful how this event here in Frankfurt has ended.” Police also used water cannon in the cities of Hamburg and Cologne after they said demonstrators targeted emergency service workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. Riot Police block the street in front of protesters after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” (Photo by KIRILL KUDRYAVTSEV / AFP) In Berlin, a protest not organised by the “GenZ regelt!” movement took place in the evening, with police reporting they were pelted with eggs and bottles. A police officer in Bonn suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group. Police were reported to have arrested large numbers of rioters. The youth-led protests earlier in the day took place in a mostly peaceful and festive atmosphere. Some people were dressed in outfits ranging from dinosaurs to Batman as the demonstrations coincided with Halloween. item.title: Army rescues 11 kidnapped victims in Kebbi operations
item.description: Troops of Sector 2, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, have rescued 11 kidnapped victims in Danko-Wasagu Local Government Area of Kebbi in two separate encounters. The operations, deployed for counter-terrorism and anti-banditry, took place on Oct. 30 and 31. The Acting Deputy Director of Army Public Relations for 8 Division, Nigerian Army, Lt-Col. Osoba Olaniyi, confirmed this in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria in Birnin Kebbi on Sunday. He revealed that: “in the first operation, the troops responded to a distress call reporting that armed bandits have blocked a road leading to Ribah town and attempted to enter the town. “On arrival, troops found that an unspecified number of civilians have been kidnapped and some motorcycles were abandoned at the scene. “Troops immediately pursued the bandits and exchanged fire with them, forcing them to abandon seven kidnapped victims.” Olaniyi listed the rescued victims as Sa’adu Bala, Dantani Yahyi, Nura Musa, Nasiru Muhammad, Abdulakeem Abubakar, Abdulahi Maikudi and Zaki Gom. The acting director said the rescued persons had been reunited with their families. Speaking on the second operation, Olaniyi said the troops were on patrol in the Wasagu area when they came under fire from terrorists. “The troops responded decisively, forcing the terrorists to flee and abandon four victims who had earlier been abducted from their farms in Wasagu village. “The rescued victims were Lawali Ali, Samaila Shuaibu, Kasimu Shuaibu and Aliyu Bala, all of Wasagu village. They were handed over to the community head,” he said. Olaniyi reiterated the determination of the troops to the safety and security of all communities in the area, assuring that they would continue to respond promptly to security threats. item.title: 5 bright planets to spot in November — when and where to see them
item.description: null This is a great month for planet watching, either in the evenings or mornings. During convenient evening hours, the planet of choice is Saturn , visible well up in the southern sky during mid-to-late evening hours. Telescopically, the southern side of its famous ring system is currently tilted about 6½ degrees to our line of sight. Around the middle of the night, Mars and Jupiter come into view above the east-northeast horizon and just before the break of dawn are in excellent position, soaring high in the southern sky in the vicinity of the Sickle of Leo the Lion. Watch how Mars approaches Jupiter early in the month, passes it on Nov. 16, then spends the rest of the month sailing away to the east. Meanwhile, in the predawn morning sky, Venus literally vaults into prominence as the month progresses. And from midmonth on through the end of November, Mercury asserts itself, appearing as a very bright "star" to the far lower left of Venus. In our schedule, remember that when measuring the angular separation between two celestial objects, your clenched fist held at arm's length measures roughly 10 degrees. Here, we present a schedule below which provides some of the best planet viewing times as well directing you as to where to look to see them Reminder: On Nov. 1 — where applicable — change clocks back one hour from Daylight Saving Time. On this date, the clock hour from 1 to 2:00 a.m. is repeated, thus making this day the longest of the year: 25 hours long. The mnemonic is: " Spring Ahead, Fall Back." Mercury Mercury, hidden during inferior conjunction with the sun on Nov. 4, will emerge in the eastern morning sky after the second week of the month to undergo an excellent morning apparition for the Northern Hemisphere. This rocky little world arrives at its greatest western elongation (20 degrees) from the sun on Nov. 20; its most favorable morning apparition of the year for mid-northern observers. From Nov. 16 to Nov. 26 speedy Mercury will rise in the east-southeast before the beginning of astronomical twilight, more than 95 minutes before sunrise. Venus Venus is a good reason to be up at the crack of dawn in November; it's a silvery lamp that rises above the east-southeast horizon. Venus was at inferior conjunction on Oct. 24. But the steep angle of the ecliptic at dawn in late autumn helps Venus vault noticeably higher with each passing day for observers at mid-northern latitudes. On Nov. 1, it rises 55 minutes before the sun. But just several days later on Nov. 5, viewers around 40 degrees north latitude can see Venus come up one hour and 25 minutes before the sun and shine 15 degrees above the horizon at sunrise. As November ends, Venus rises nearly 3½ hours before the sun and hangs nearly 35 degrees up at sunrise. All month Venus brightens impressively and on the penultimate day of the month it will reach the pinnacle of its magnificent brightness, shining at magnitude -4.9, rising almost 3½ hours before the sun. item.title: Youth Olympic Games kick off in Dakar
item.description: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games have officially kicked off in Senegal. Crowds gathered for Saturday's opening ceremony, featuring hundreds of drummers and dancers celebrating Senegalese and wider African culture, in keeping with the Games' motto: “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates”. It is the first-ever Olympic sporting event to be held on the African continent, but comes as Senegal faces an economic crisis. The country's president has said he wants to turn sport into an “economic and social engine”. The Games also come amid a government crackdown on LGBTQ+ people. Nearly 3,000 teenagers from more than 200 countries are competing in around a dozen sports, including athletics, beach wrestling and a five-a-side version of baseball. Jean-Loup Chappelet, Professor at Lausanne University and Olympics specialist, shares further insights.

The governor was dressed by Nigerian designer Ugo Monye in regal off-white attire that blended the traditional caftan with a kimono-inspired design. He completed the look with a beige fedora. Sanwo-Olu walked confidently across the runway, drawing applause from the audience as he flashed peace signs and exchanged nods with spectators. I stepped away from the usual business of governance to walk the runway for the incredibly talented Ugo Monye at Lagos Fashion Week. Lagos continues to grow as a home for fashion, creativity and culture and I am always happy to support the people driving this growth. pic.twitter.com/B1tnMiiSoh — Babajide Sanwo-Olu (@jidesanwoolu) October 31, 2026 The 2026 Lagos Fashion Week, themed “CRAFTED: Heritage”, began last Wednesday at the Federal Palace Hotel in Lagos and is scheduled to end on Sunday. The annual fashion event brings together designers, models, industry professionals and fashion enthusiasts to celebrate African creativity, craftsmanship and heritage. item.title: Obi accuses Tinubu of neglecting Imo, cites insecurity, poverty
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has accused President Bola Tinubu of neglecting Imo State, alleging that the President has not spent a night in the state since assuming office despite spending more than 260 days abroad. Obi made the allegation during a town hall meeting in Owerri, Imo State, on Saturday, October 31, 2026, as part of his ongoing nationwide engagement with Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement posted on his X handle on Sunday, Obi said he had earlier visited a market in Owerri, where he interacted with traders, buyers and other residents about their economic challenges. He said their accounts reflected the difficulties ordinary Nigerians were facing under the economic policies of the Tinubu administration. At the town hall meeting, the former Anambra State governor criticised the Federal Government over what he described as rising national debt without corresponding improvements in citizens’ living conditions. He also raised concerns about poverty, hunger, insecurity and out-of-school children, claiming that more than 140 million Nigerians were living in multidimensional poverty, while approximately 18 million children were out of school. Obi further described Nigeria as one of the world’s most terrorised countries, arguing that the country was facing multiple economic and security challenges. Reassuring residents that the country could overcome its challenges, the NDC candidate said he and his running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, were committed to securing and uniting the country. He also pledged massive investments in critical sectors, particularly healthcare and education, as well as policies aimed at lifting millions of Nigerians out of poverty. Obi said the duo possessed the experience, competence, capacity and commitment required to address the country’s challenges. During the interactive session, he said participants also raised questions about the protection of their votes in the 2027 elections. He urged voters to turn out in large numbers, exercise their democratic rights and remain at their polling units until the final results were declared. Obi expressed appreciation to his supporters, party candidates, members and organisers, as well as residents of Imo State, for their reception and support. He described the task of building a new Nigeria as a collective responsibility, expressing optimism that the country could work for all its citizens. The post Obi accuses Tinubu of neglecting Imo, cites insecurity, poverty appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: South-East ready to return Tinubu, Shettima, Kalu claims
item.description: The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Okezie Kalu, has claimed that the South-East has resolved to support the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima in 2027. Kalu said the region was prepared to return the APC-led administration for another term in appreciation of what he described as Tinubu’s support for the Igbo people. He spoke on Saturday at the flag-off of the APC Women’s Mobilisation Campaign and South-East Women Empowerment Programme, organised by the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, in Enugu. The Deputy Speaker, who is also the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council 11 (South), said the immediate political responsibility of the Igbo people was to support a leader who, according to him, had demonstrated commitment to their interests. He recalled that Tinubu, during his tenure as governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007, appointed Igbo people into his administration. “This man has not hidden his love for Ndi Igbo. During his time as the governor of Lagos State, no Igbo property was taken. Nobody who was a businessman in Lagos was arrested. Mr Ben Akabueze was an Igbo man that he brought into his cabinet as governor. It has never happened before. I hope we will reciprocate his kind gestures to Ndi Igbo. We must do so this time,” he said. Kalu also recalled the post-civil war promise of Reconstruction, Rehabilitation and Reintegration (3Rs), arguing that successive administrations had failed to fulfil the commitment to the people of the South-East until Tinubu assumed office. He cited the signing into law of the South-East Development Commission Bill as evidence of the President’s commitment to the region. “I also need to remind you that after the civil war, we waited for almost 60 years for a promise that was made to the people of Igbo land that was not kept. The 3Rs: Reconciliation, Reconstruction and Reintegration. Was the promise kept or not? It wasn’t kept. “Government after government but they ignored us. Administration after administration, they ignored the Igbo and we were waiting and asking, when will the messiah come to save the Igbo? Then came a man who loves the Igbo from his heart,” he said. The Deputy Speaker added that the South-East Development Commission Bill had remained pending through successive assemblies before Tinubu signed it into law. “South-East Development Commission Bill has been in the Parliament from year to year, Assembly to Assembly, they refused to sign it into law. But when President Tinubu came, South-East Development Commission became a commission under the law. Tinubu is a warrior, a great President,” he added. Kalu further listed road construction, bridge projects, scholarships and loans among the interventions he said the Federal Government had undertaken in the region, while commending the First Lady for her women’s empowerment initiatives.
